news1Benefit3: Overload protection: automatic shutdown in case of breakdown risk. Why is MOTIX IMD700A better? Reduces energy loss by 30% compared to traditional systems;
news1Benefit4: Suitable for all EVs — from city cars to trucks;

news3Title: Photonic Chip for Quantum Communication: Scalable Quantum Photonics
news3Paragraph1: Integrated quantum photonics is a technology for quantum operations with single photons directly on silicon chips.
news3Paragraph2: This is a key step toward creating compact, efficient, and affordable quantum networks.
news3Subtitle1: Main components of the photonic chip:
news3Item1: Quantum photon sources. From microcrystals (QDs) to ring resonators.
news3Item2: Phase shifters. Phase control is essential for quantum algorithms.
news3Item3: Single-photon detectors (SNSPD). Maximum sensitivity and speed.
news3Item4: Optical waveguides and combiners. Enable scaling and integration.
news3Benefit1: Miniaturization: devices the size of a fingernail, no excess space;
news3Benefit2: Resistant to vibrations and temperature changes;
news3Benefit3: Manufacturing: chips can be mass-produced like CMOS.
news3Project1: GKP chip in Nature  for qubit encoding. An optical "grid" of photons was formed on the chip (Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill states), similar to a chessboard. This grid is error-resistant and can be used for quantum computing and communication;
news3Project2: TFLN programmable routers — Twente/CUHK . A chip based on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), programmable for tasks from signal processing to secure radar...
news3Project3: Mass photon sources — up to 20 atomic lasers per chip...
news3Subtitle4: Why is this critical for industry?
news3Importance1: Quantum security: encryption that can't be eavesdropped;
news3Importance2: Blazing fast communication: no delays or interference — for finance, medicine, IoT;
news3Importance3: Chip-scale integration: compact chip boards instead of bulky platforms.
news3Timeline2: 2028–2030 — pilot delivery to datacenters and fintech.
news3Conclusion: The photonic chip is not just an experiment. It's the foundation for quantum internet, secure communication, and new computing architectures. For engineers — a step into quantum reality. For buyers — an innovation ready for today’s products.

news2TitleSeptember: Vorago VA5 — Dual-Core Space Microcontrollers with Built-in Intelligence
news2Paragraph1September: Electronics in space operate under special laws. Radiation, extreme temperatures, and the lack of repair possibilities all require components to have a margin of safety unattainable in conventional industrial solutions.
news3TitleSeptember: X-HBM from NEO Semiconductor: A Breakthrough in Memory for AI Chips
news3Paragraph1September: In early August, NEO Semiconductor announced Extreme High Bandwidth Memory (X-HBM) — a memory architecture that promises not just an evolution, but a qualitatively new approach.
news4Intro: Renesas has introduced a new line of RL78/L23 microcontrollers. These are 16-bit MCUs designed with a focus on ultra-low power consumption and built-in support for user interfaces - segment LCDs and capacitive sensors.
news4Problem: Many devices today need to be 'always on', battery-powered, and have a simple but convenient interface.
news4Solution: This is where RL78/L23 meets the need: they save energy, and the built-in display and sensor controller eliminates external components, reducing cost and development complexity.
news4Feature2: up to 512 KB flash with dual-bank architecture, allowing firmware updates without stopping the device
news4Feature3: built-in segment LCD controller and capacitive touch up to 36 channels
news4Feature4: power supply range from 1.6 V to 5.5 V, providing options for battery solutions and standard sources
news4Feature5: sleep and power saving modes extend the life of autonomous devices
news4Temperature: Operating temperature range from -40 °C to +105 °C makes RL78/L23 suitable for household appliances, climate control equipment and industrial conditions.
news4Applications: This MCU series simplifies the creation of IoT devices, smart appliances and meters. The display driver and touch controller are pre-installed. Support for FOTA and dual-bank memory ensures that devices can be updated without stopping operation.
news4Audience1: manufacturers of household electronics and smart home devices
news4Audience2: developers of IoT sensors and autonomous systems
news4Audience3: companies that value long-term energy savings and simple interface implementation
news4Conclusion: Renesas RL78/L23 is a step towards simpler and more reliable solutions where autonomy, basic visualization and minimal energy consumption are required.
news5Intro: Electronics in space operate under special laws. Radiation, extreme temperatures, lack of repair possibilities — all this requires components to have a margin of safety unattainable in conventional industrial solutions.
news5Context: This is why the emergence of new microcontrollers from Vorago Technologies has sparked interest among space system developers.
news5ProductDesc: The company introduced the VA5 Dual-Core SpaceGrade MCU family — the first controllers of their class with dual-core ARM Cortex-M55 architecture and built-in artificial intelligence module (Ethos-U55 NPU). This combination opens the way for onboard data processing in spacecraft: from machine vision to autonomous navigation.
news5Feature1: The main difference of the VA5 series is its focus on 'smart' tasks. The built-in neuroprocessor allows executing machine learning algorithms locally, reducing dependence on ground centers.
news5Feature2: At the same time, the controllers are designed to operate in conditions of increased radiation and temperature fluctuations, making them suitable for orbital missions and interplanetary projects.
news5DualCore: Another feature is dual-core architecture. One processor handles critical functions (control systems, security), while the other processes 'heavy' data and neural network calculations. This approach enhances reliability and enables efficient resource distribution.
news5DevTools: For developers, Vorago offers not only chips but also a complete set of tools: SDK, modeling tools, and certification support for space standards. This means the new microcontrollers are ready for integration into real projects — from small satellites to complex research platforms.
news5MarketImpactTitle: What does this mean for the market?
news5MarketImpact: The emergence of VA5 shows that space electronics is rapidly catching up with 'earthly' trends — AI and parallel computing. Engineers can now design smarter and more autonomous systems without compromising between reliability and performance.
news6Intro: As the load for generative AI models grows, memory limits and bandwidth become bottlenecks. Traditional HBM solutions are approaching their limits: complexity, cost, power consumption.
news6Announcement: In these conditions, NEO Semiconductor announced Extreme High Bandwidth Memory (X-HBM) in early August - a memory architecture that promises not just evolution, but a qualitatively new approach.
news6Feature1: X-HBM offers a 32-kilobit data bus and potential density of up to 512 Gbit per die.
news6Comparison: For comparison: the expected HBM5 (which is still in development) focuses on buses of about 4 K-bit and densities of about 40 Gbit.
news6Advantage: Thus X-HBM provides either 16 times greater bandwidth or 10 times higher density than traditional HBM solutions.
news6Technology: The architecture is built on NEO's original 3D X-DRAM technology, which allows bypassing many limitations inherent in classical DRAM and HBM approaches.
news6GameChangerTitle: Why X-HBM could be a game changer

news6Scalability: Increasing data bus width and memory density allows reducing latency and facilitating scaling.

news_oct7_description: Analog Devices introduced 18 low-power ADCs that convert analog sensor signals to digital without loss of accuracy while consuming minimal power.
adc_solution_for: Analog Devices has introduced a lineup of 18 new low-power ADCs (analog-to-digital converters). These are components that convert sensor signals (such as sound, pressure, or temperature) into digital form for processing by microcontrollers. The distinctive feature of these solutions is that they are designed for minimal power consumption while maintaining accuracy.
adc_feature_iot_sensors: IoT sensors In Internet of Things systems, each device often operates on a limited power source. Reducing ADC power consumption extends device lifespan to several years without battery replacement. This is crucial when sensors are installed in hard-to-reach locations - for example, on industrial equipment or infrastructure objects.
adc_feature_medical_devices: Medical devices In portable diagnostics, measurement accuracy is key. Electrocardiographs, glucometers, and health monitoring devices must remain compact and energy-efficient. The new Analog Devices ADCs allow data collection without quality loss, maintaining device size, and increasing battery life.
adc_feature_wearable_electronics: Wearable electronics Fitness bracelets, smart watches, and other gadgets are becoming full-fledged measuring stations. They monitor heart rate, movement, sleep quality, and in the future - more complex parameters. That's why the transition to low-power components, including ADCs, is becoming a decisive factor.
adc_feature_technical_context: New Analog Devices converters provide balance between three parameters:
adc_before_engineers: Previously, engineers had to sacrifice one of these parameters: high accuracy usually meant increased energy consumption. Now this compromise is gradually being eliminated - chip design technologies allow reducing power consumption without loss in measurement quality.
adc_trend_mobile_systems: Implementation of low-power solutions reflects the industry's general direction: from large stationary systems to mobile, autonomous, and distributed ones. If previously electronics mainly depended on grid power, today the main growth is provided by devices that must operate 'in the field', away from power outlets. Low power consumption is becoming not only an advantage but also a condition for product market entry.
adc_trend_market_growth: The emergence of autonomous devices and distributed systems stimulates demand for energy-efficient components.
adc_conclusion: The appearance of 18 new Analog Devices ADCs is a step towards creating an ecosystem of components where every detail is designed for long autonomous operation. This opens new opportunities for engineers and companies: to design devices that will be compact, energy-efficient, and yet accurate.
adc_last_conclusion: In the coming years, such solutions will form the basis for new-generation medical devices, wearable electronics, and millions of IoT sensors.
news_14_oct_Intro1: We are used to computers responding to keystrokes or mouse movements. Now a new level of interaction is emerging — when the device «sees» that there is a person nearby.
news_14_oct_Intro2: STMicroelectronics has introduced Human Presence Detection (HPD) technology. At its core is the ToF sensor (Time-of-Flight) VL53L8CP, which measures distance using laser pulses, and artificial intelligence algorithms.
news_14_oct_Context1: Together, they allow a laptop or other device to «notice» the user. The operation of the ToF sensor is as follows: a laser emitter sends invisible and eye-safe infrared light with a wavelength of 940 nm, which reflects off surfaces. The sensor measures the time it takes for the light to travel to the object and back, and based on this data determines the distance.
news_14_oct_ProductDesc: What does this mean in practice?
news_14_oct_Feature1: The screen turns off if you walk away from the desk.
news_14_oct_Feature2: The system locks («walk-away lock») when you leave your workspace.
news_14_oct_Feature3: The device tracks head position and gestures, adapting to your movements.
news_14_oct_DevTools1: The main effect is energy savings. The screen and processor work only when it's really necessary. For manufacturers, this is a chance to make laptops and PCs «green» and convenient, while for users — to get comfort and additional data protection.
news_14_oct_DevTools2: Interestingly, ST has gone beyond classical infrared sensors. Thanks to the combination of ToF sensor and AI, the device can not only detect presence but also distinguish context: for example, to dim the screen when the user looks away. Or detect when another person is looking over the user's shoulder.
news_14_oct_MarketImpact1: The problem of displays and computers left on when no one is using them is not new. According to a 2004 report by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in the United States, «nighttime audits of office buildings showed that 64 percent of computers and 82 percent of LCD monitors remained on overnight».
news_14_oct_MarketImpact2: The study doesn't specify how many of them were locked and required user authentication, but we can reasonably assume that some of them could be used without entering a password. This is not only a huge waste of energy but also means these systems are vulnerable to evil maid attacks.
news_14_oct_MarketImpact3: In conditions where electronics power consumption is becoming a global challenge, such solutions could change industry standards. HPD is called the «invisible function of the future» — we won't notice its operation but will constantly benefit from its results.
news_21_oct_Intro1: At the PCIM and APEC 2025 exhibitions, Texas Instruments presented the latest developments in power management. These are new electronic components for high-load systems — data centers, servers, and artificial intelligence equipment.
news_21_oct_Intro2: TI demonstrates that the transition to new energy efficiency standards is already becoming an industrial reality.
news_21_oct_Image: Image provided by: TI. Placement TI1685.
news_21_oct_MainFocus: The main focus is on two directions:
news_21_oct_Direction2: GaN power stages in industrial TOLL packaging with different resistances (35 mΩ, 25 mΩ, etc.).
news_21_oct_Context: Modern data centers and AI systems operate with enormous currents and power. Conventional fuses and power transistors can no longer handle this. Solutions based on GaN (gallium nitride) provide:
news_21_oct_Benefit1: Efficiency: GaN stages deliver efficiency up to 98%, while traditional silicon solutions typically remain in the 90-94% range.
news_21_oct_Benefit2: Dimensions: due to operation at higher frequencies, GaN power modules allow reducing the size of inductors and capacitors, shrinking the power board by almost 30-40%.
news_21_oct_Benefit3: Heating: on-resistance (Rds(on)) of GaN is lower — for example, 25-35 mΩ compared to typical 50-70 mΩ for silicon MOSFETs, which reduces thermal losses by almost half.
news_21_oct_Benefit4: Frequency: GaN transistors reliably operate at frequencies of hundreds of kHz and above, where silicon already faces increasing losses and switching limitations.
news_21_oct_SmartFuse: And the «smart fuse» TPS1685 adds intelligent protection functions — against short circuits, overloads, and overheating. Essentially, it's an electronic fuse with monitoring that can «disconnect» the circuit in time and thereby protect expensive systems.
news_21_oct_ValuePoints: For engineers and procurement specialists, these components mean:
news_21_oct_Value1: reduction in energy consumption of servers and network equipment;
news_21_oct_Value2: increased reliability and lifespan of systems;
news_21_oct_Value3: reduction in cooling and maintenance costs.
news_21_oct_TechnologyScope: Technologies of GaN transistors and eFuse fuses are becoming basic elements not only for data centers but also for telecommunications, electric vehicles, and industrial automation.
news_21_oct_Conclusion: TI's entry into the market with ready-made industrial solutions shows: GaN electronics is no longer an experiment but a working tool for major players. In the coming years, such components will determine how economical and reliable new servers, fast charging stations, and industrial controllers will be.

news_nov14_title_news_page: Liquid Metal and Polymers: A Step Towards Flexible and Recyclable Electronics
liquid_metal_paragraph2: Scientists have introduced a new material that could change the approach to flexible electronics manufacturing. This is a recyclable composite based on liquid metal and a stretchable polymer, which was purposefully developed as a multifunctional platform.
liquid_metal_paragraph3: The material features high conductivity, resistance to deformation, and the possibility of secondary recycling.
liquid_metal_paragraph4: The technology combines droplets of liquid metal - gallium and indium - with a polymer matrix. When damaged, the material can "self-heal", and after disposal - be recycled without loss of properties.
liquid_metal_paragraph6: Modern devices - from smartphones to industrial sensors - consist of dozens of incompatible materials: metals, plastics, adhesives. This makes them almost unsuitable for recycling. The new composite solves this problem: when heated and mechanically processed, the liquid metal separates from the polymer, and both phases can be reused.
liquid_metal_paragraph7: For manufacturers, this is not just a laboratory experiment, but a new direction in designing sustainable electronic systems. If previously flexible circuits required sacrificing reliability or electrical conductivity, now it's possible to create components that withstand bending, stretching, and multiple usage cycles without degradation.
liquid_metal_paragraph9: The application of such materials opens prospects in several directions:
liquid_metal_paragraph10: Wearable electronics - bracelets, medical sensors, smart textiles;
liquid_metal_paragraph11: Industrial sensors - flexible elements for monitoring vibration, temperature, leaks;
liquid_metal_paragraph12: Robotics - adaptive surfaces and connections capable of mimicking structural shapes.
liquid_metal_paragraph13: For companies working in flexible electronics and environmental technologies, the material creates a foundation for new products with closed life cycles - from production to reuse.
liquid_metal_paragraph15: The development of such materials reflects a trend important for the entire industry: moving away from disposable electronic devices. The concept of "built-in recyclability" is gradually transitioning from laboratories to prototypes of commercial products. This is no longer a matter of fashion, but an economic calculation - reducing disposal costs, meeting environmental requirements, and increasing customer trust.
liquid_metal_paragraph17: The liquid metal composite from the University of Washington demonstrates that material innovations can change the very philosophy of electronics. Flexibility, repairability, and recyclability are becoming not a compromise, but the norm. For the B2B market, this is a signal to prepare for new standards - where reliability and sustainability go hand in hand.

sony_paragraph1: Automotive surveillance systems are becoming increasingly complex. Cameras no longer just capture images — they operate as part of driver assistance systems, evaluating distances, movement, light, and contrast.
sony_paragraph2: At the same time, every microchip, every interface affects the module size, power consumption, and reliability of the entire system.

news_dec21_para1: Power electronics is evolving around high power and compactness challenges. Against this background, 1200 V components occupy an important place.This is the voltage level used by inverters, charging stations, power systems and industrial drives.

news_dec21_subtitle1: What is SiC and why 1200 V is important
news_dec21_para3: SiC is silicon carbide. The material withstands high temperatures and reduces losses in electronics operation. Therefore, SiC MOSFETs are well suited for applications where the device operates under load for a long time.
news_dec21_para4: Wolfspeed introduced Gen 4 power SiC modules in a six-pack configuration. These are three-phase power modules used in drives, industrial invertersand electric transport systems. The module already contains the entire power section, making it easier for engineers to design the circuit.
news_dec21_para5: A separate direction is 1200 V SiC diodes and 1200 V SiC rectifiers.A SiC diode has almost no reverse recovery, it "switches" faster between modes. This reduces heating and energy losses.
news_dec21_para6: This approach is useful in high-frequency circuits, power supplies and power factor correction systems. Small packages like DPAK save board space and make devices more compact.
news_dec21_para7: GaN is gallium nitride. The technology is actively developing, and onsemi has revealed the vertical GaN-on-GaN technology, where current flows vertically through the crystal. This approach increases voltage strength (up to and above 1200 V), reduces switching losses and allows reducing the size of power platforms.
news_dec21_para8: Such solutions are interesting for data centers, charging infrastructure and inverters for solar systems. The main idea is more power in a smaller volume.
news_dec21_para9: The increase in AI infrastructure power, the growth of the electric vehicle market (including passenger models, commercial transport, charging infrastructure and supply chains: batteries, power electronics, sensors, control systems), the transition to distributed energy generation — all this encourages engineers to use SiC MOSFETs, GaN, SiC diodes and 1200 V power modules.
news_dec21_para10: Such components help create compact inverters, increase power density, improve thermal management and increase energy efficiency.

news_dec14_para1: High-voltage transformer is the basis of many systems: from industrial electronics to charging stations and power equipment. The key nodes of such a circuit operate at high currents and frequencies, so the elements must be stable and safe.
news_dec14_para2: Here, MLCCs with C0G dielectric play their role — ceramic capacitors with a high level of stability.

news_dec14_para9: For the market, this means more layout options, compactness and increased device lifespan. This means that power electronics can move towards smaller dimensions, high power density and resistance to loads without compromising safety.

news_page_feb21_title: Snapdragon X2 Plus: New ARM Platform for Laptops and AI Devices
news_feb21_para1: The ARM processor market for PCs continues to evolve. The Snapdragon X2 Plus platform expands the presence of ARM architecture in the segment of laptops, workstations and AI devices, where classical x86 solutions previously dominated.
news_feb21_para2: The development vector is obvious: energy efficiency, local data processing and integration of AI functions at the hardware platform level.
news_feb21_para3: Snapdragon X2 Plus is a system-on-chip (SoC) for PCs and mobile workstations, focused on devices running Windows on ARM and AI-oriented platforms. The architecture is built around ARM cores with integration of a neural processor (NPU), graphics accelerator and memory controllers in a single chip.
news_feb21_para4: The key feature is the focus not only on performance, but also on sustainable operation with low power consumption, which is critical for ultra-thin laptops, mobile workstations and edge devices.
news_feb21_para5: The platform architecture emphasizes three directions:
news_feb21_list_item1:
Local AI processing
The presence of a built-in NPU allows performing machine learning tasks without accessing cloud services. This reduces latency and network load, which is important for corporate AI applications, analytics and automation.
news_feb21_list_item2:
Energy efficiency of ARM architecture
Compared to classical x86 platforms, ARM solutions provide lower power consumption for comparable office, multimedia and AI workloads. This translates into increased battery life and reduced thermal requirements for device design.
news_feb21_list_item3:
Component integration
The SoC approach simplifies device development: CPU, GPU, NPU and controllers are in one chip. This reduces board complexity, energy losses and cooling requirements.
news_feb21_subtitle3: Where it is applicable in practice
news_feb21_para6: Snapdragon X2 Plus is focused on several segments:
news_feb21_list_item7: edge devices for industrial automation and data analytics.
news_feb21_para7: In the corporate environment, this is especially relevant for local data processing tasks, analytics, document workflow, intelligent assistants and decision support systems.
news_feb21_subtitle4: Why this is important for the electronics market
news_feb21_para8: The development of ARM platforms for PCs creates an alternative ecosystem to the x86 architecture. This reduces dependence on one class of processors, expands choice for device manufacturers and gives developers new hardware capabilities for AI applications and energy-efficient systems.
news_feb21_para9: Snapdragon X2 Plus shows the market direction: integration of AI accelerators into the basic processor architecture and shifting focus towards local data processing, autonomy and systemic energy efficiency.
news_page_feb14_title: ARTERY-KY Microcontrollers as a Platform for IoT and Edge Analytics
news_feb14_para1: Microcontrollers still remain the foundation of embedded electronics. The ARTERY-KY line of 32-bit MCUs is focused on IoT systems, edge devices and smart electronics, where energy efficiency and integration flexibility are important.
news_feb14_para2: For industrial electronics and commercial devices, the balance between performance, power consumption and integration cost becomes key.
news_feb14_subtitle1: Architecture logic: not 'more powerful', but 'more rational'
news_feb14_para3: ARTERY-KY uses a 32-bit architecture, which compared to 8- and 16-bit MCUs provides:
news_feb14_list_item3: support for complex control and analytics algorithms.
news_feb14_para4: For example, processing data arrays and signal filtering are performed in fewer clock cycles than on 8-bit controllers, which directly affects system response speed and operational stability.
news_feb14_subtitle2: What makes these MCUs practical for developers
news_feb14_list_item4:
Edge computing support
Ability to perform basic analytics and data processing locally, without transmission to the cloud. This reduces latency and load on communication channels.
news_feb14_list_item5:
Flexible peripherals
Support for interfaces for working with sensors, actuators and communication modules (SPI, I²C, UART, CAN — depending on the model).
news_feb14_list_item6:
Optimized power consumption
Compared to universal 32-bit MCUs, controllers with low-power modes allow extending autonomous operation of devices — especially relevant for IoT sensors and autonomous nodes.
news_feb14_subtitle4: Why this is important for the electronics market
news_feb14_para6: The emergence of new 32-bit MCU platforms expands choice for developers and reduces dependence on a limited circle of manufacturers. This forms a more sustainable component ecosystem and provides the market with alternative architectural solutions.
news_feb14_para7: ARTERY-KY demonstrates the transition to universal microcontrollers that are focused not on maximum frequencies, but on systemic efficiency, integration and practical applicability.

news_page_mar14_title: Nordic Semiconductor and the Development of Edge AI Devices
news_mar14_para1: The Internet of Things is growing rapidly, and with it the volume of transmitted data increases. To reduce the load on the cloud and transmission delays, information processing on the device itself is used — an approach known as Edge AI.
news_mar14_para2: Instead of sending the full data stream to the server, the device analyzes information locally and transmits only the processing result or events.
news_mar14_para3: This approach is especially in demand in systems with limited power consumption and unstable communication.
news_mar14_para4: Nordic Semiconductor is developing solutions for Edge AI based on its energy-efficient systems-on-chip (SoC) with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) support. These chips are used in IoT devices due to low power consumption and stable wireless communication.
news_mar14_subtitle1: Why Edge AI is becoming in demand
news_mar14_para5: The classical IoT architecture involves constant data transmission to the cloud. In practice, this creates several problems:
news_mar14_list_item1: increased power consumption of the radio channel
news_mar14_para6: If part of the analysis is performed directly on the device, the volume of transmitted data is significantly reduced.
news_mar14_para7: Nordic platforms combine several components necessary for local data processing:
news_mar14_list_item4: BLE radio interface for communication with other devices
news_mar14_list_item5: ARM processor core with support for digital signal processing instructions
news_mar14_list_item6: development tools for integrating compact machine learning models (TinyML)
news_mar14_para8: In such an architecture, the device analyzes the sensor data stream locally and transmits only significant events. For example, a motion sensor can send a signal only when activity is detected, rather than transmitting a continuous stream of measurements.
news_mar14_para9: Edge AI is already used in various segments:
news_mar14_list_item9: monitoring and diagnostic systems for machinery
news_mar14_para10: For developers, this means that part of the computing is transferred from servers directly to devices. As a result, requirements for cloud infrastructure are reduced and the battery life of IoT nodes increases.
news_mar14_para11: Conclusion: local data processing is gradually becoming a standard element of IoT architecture. Edge AI allows reducing delays, lowering power consumption and increasing device autonomy.
news_page_mar07_title: Kyocera mmWave Sensor for Precise Object Detection
news_mar07_para1: Millimeter radio waves are increasingly being used in object detection and distance measurement systems. Such sensors operate independently of lighting conditions and can maintain measurement stability in difficult weather conditions.
news_mar07_para2: Kyocera Corporation has introduced a module with an mmWave sensor, focused on industrial automation and transportation systems tasks.
news_mar07_para3: mmWave sensors use millimeter-wave radio waves — typically tens of gigahertz. The signal is emitted by the sensor, reflected from the object and returns back. Based on the parameters of the reflected signal, the system determines distance, speed and movement.
news_mar07_para5: Compared to optical sensors, the radio frequency method is independent of lighting. Unlike ultrasonic sensors, millimeter radars typically provide greater measurement range and are insensitive to acoustic environmental noise.
news_mar07_subtitle2: Where mmWave sensors can be applied
news_mar07_para6: The technology is gradually finding application in various areas:
news_mar07_list_item4: driver assistance systems and transport safety
news_mar07_para7: In these tasks, reliable object detection under various lighting conditions and in polluted environments is important.
news_mar07_para8: The presented module is focused on integration into embedded systems and industrial electronics devices. Key characteristics include:
news_mar07_list_item9: possibility of integration with existing controllers
news_mar07_list_item10: resistance to dust and contamination, which is important for industrial conditions
news_mar07_para9: For developers, this means the ability to add object detection functionality without switching to more complex and expensive systems such as lidars.
news_mar07_para10: mmWave sensors are gradually expanding their application area in detection and distance measurement systems. The radio frequency method allows increasing the stability of sensors in real operating conditions.

news_page_apr14_title: SiC Power Modules Are Shaping a New Architecture for Energy Converters

news_apr14_para2: While SiC was previously used mainly in high-voltage nodes, two classes of solutions have now simultaneously entered the market:

news_apr14_para4: Current new products can be divided into two technological levels.
news_apr14_para5: The first level is integrated molded modules.
news_apr14_para6: In such packages, power chips are combined with drivers, protections and optimized current path layout. This reduces the number of external components and reduces development complexity.
news_apr14_para7: The engineering effect is immediately visible in several parameters:

news_apr14_para8: Reducing parasitic parameters directly affects switching losses. By increasing the frequency, the size of magnetic components and filters can be reduced, which reduces the dimensions of power supplies and inverters.
news_apr14_para9: The second level is high-power SiC power modules.
news_apr14_para10: These solutions are focused on systems of tens of kilowatts and megawatt-class: renewable energy inverters, traction drives, charging infrastructure.
news_apr14_para11: The key difference is related not to electrical parameters, but to packaging technologies.

news_page_apr07_title: GaN and AlN Transistors Are Changing Power and Radio Frequency Electronics
news_apr07_para1: The growth of computing, communication networks and mobile devices is increasing demands on power electronics. The industry is simultaneously developing GaN transistors and a new class of AlN structures, which increase frequencies, efficiency and power density.
news_apr07_para2: Power electronics is undergoing a change of materials. Gallium nitride is already actively used in power supplies and chargers.
news_apr07_para3: In parallel, a new class of transistors based on aluminum nitride is emerging, focused on radio frequency systems. Both technologies solve a similar problem — to increase energy conversion efficiency and operation at high frequencies.
news_apr07_subtitle1: GaN in power supplies and chargers
news_apr07_para4: GaN transistors are capable of operating at significantly higher switching frequencies compared to silicon MOSFETs. In practice, this means reducing the size of magnetic components and increasing power supply efficiency.
news_apr07_para6: Increasing the switching frequency several times allows reducing the dimensions of transformers and chokes. Magnetic components occupy most of the volume of power supplies.
news_apr07_para8: The next step in development is XHEMT transistors based on the AlN/GaN/AlN structure.
news_apr07_para9: The first generation of devices already demonstrates specific performance indicators:
news_apr07_para10: The high thermal conductivity of AlN reduces thermal resistance and improves stability at high power.
news_apr07_subtitle3: Specific market new products: what manufacturers have already introduced
news_apr07_para12: The development of GaN and new RF technologies has already moved from laboratories to commercial products. Over the past year, major power electronics manufacturers have introduced new generations of transistors and platforms focused on server power supplies, telecom and high-power chargers.
news_apr07_para13: Infineon has expanded its CoolGaN G5 line. The new transistors are rated for 650 V and are designed for server power supplies and high-power chargers.
news_apr07_para14: Key changes in the G5 generation:
news_apr07_list_item14: reduction of dynamic switching losses by approximately 20–30%
news_apr07_list_item16: increase in permissible switching frequency up to hundreds of kilohertz
news_apr07_para15: The practical effect is an increase in power density of server power supplies and a reduction in the size of magnetic components.
news_apr07_subtitle5: Navitas — integrated GaN power ICs GaNSense
news_apr07_para16: Navitas continues to develop the GaN Power IC concept, where the transistor, driver and protection are combined in one package.

news_apr07_para18: Driver integration reduces the number of external components and reduces board area. Compared to a discrete circuit, the number of components can be reduced by 30–40%.

news_apr07_para21: High frequency allows reducing inductors and capacitors several times, which directly affects the dimensions of power boards.

news_apr07_para22: Transphorm, together with Renesas, is developing GaN solutions for high-power power supplies.
news_apr07_para23: The new SuperGaN transistors are designed for:
news_apr07_para24: Manufacturers emphasize increased reliability and service life, which is critical for data center infrastructure.
news_apr07_subtitle8: Why this is important for the industry
news_apr07_para25: GaN is strengthening the power supply and charger market. AlN is opening up opportunities for high-frequency communication systems and radar.
news_apr07_para26: Both technologies show a common trend: the transition of power and RF electronics to wide-bandgap semiconductors.
news_apr07_para27: Wide-bandgap materials are shaping a new generation of transistors. Together, these technologies set the direction for the development of power and high-frequency systems for the coming years.
